findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Observed several food items stored in grocery store sacks in several freezers and the walk-in cooler. Grocery store sacks are not approved food-grade storage packagings. PIC was notified and staff started the process of repackaging the items using an available roll of approved food-grade bags. Ensure that food is protected from contamination by always using food-grade packaging for storage.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(4) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (4) Except as specified under Subparagraph 3-501.15(B)(2) and in (B) of this section, storing the food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings. [C]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed the kitchen hand washing sink was blocked with a bottle of soap and plastic when the inspector arrived. CORRECTED: The staff removed from the sink during the inspection. Ensure that hand washing sinks are maintained accessible for employee use at all times.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing.

findings.title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed that there was not a probe-style thermometer in the establishment. The PIC was informed and will have one available on or by a Follow Up Re-Inspection in 10 days (24 April 2026). Ensure that a food measuring device is readily available for use in measuring food temperatures.
findings.citation_text: 4-302.12 Food Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. (B) A TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE with a suitable small-diameter probe that is designed to measure the temperature of thin masses shall be provided and readily accessible to accurately measure the temperature in thin FOODS such as MEAT patties and FISH filets.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
Inspectors observed the following:
(1) a buildup of soil residues on the shelves of the walk-in cooler.
(2) underneath the prep tables on a shelf was a paint scraper with with sticky green liquid.
The PIC was notified, and made plans to clean these areas more frequently.
Ensure that non-food contact surfaces of equipment are cleaned frequently to prevent the accumulation of soil residues.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed that the mop was sitting in the water part of the mop bucket where it is unable to air dry. CORRECTED: The PIC was informed that the mop was not properly stored, and the PIC removed the mop from the mop bucket and hung it to dry. Ensure that after use mops are able to fully air dry in a place where they cannot soil walls, equipment, or supplies.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
findings.comment: Observed wet wiping cloths sitting on prep counters within the kitchen. The PIC was notified and the cloths were moved into the sanitizer bucket during the inspection. Ensure that wet wiping cloths are always stored in sanitizing solutions between uses.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D).

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed dirty water inside the mop bucket stored in the closet. The PIC stated that they last mopped this morning. During the inspection the water was dumped down the mop sink. Ensure that dirty mop water is always dumped after use.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.114 Maintaining Premises, Unnecessary Items and Litter. The PREMISES shall be free of: (A) Items that are unnecessary to the operation or maintenance of the establishment such as EQUIPMENT that is nonfunctional or no longer used; and (B) Litter.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Observed an employee wash their hands in the dump sink during the inspection. The employee was educated that hand washing must only occur in designated hand washing sinks. After the education the employee rinsed their hands for about five seconds without soap and turned off the faucet with their bare hands in the hand washing sink. The inspector stepped in again and demonstrated the proper technique with the employee. After the demonstration the employee used the proper procedure, including using soap, scrubbing hands for 10-15 seconds, and using a barrier to turn off the faucet. The PIC was reminded of the importance of the proper hand washing procedure to avoid re-contaminating clean hands. Ensure that employees always wash hands in designated hand washing sinks and utilize the proper hand washing procedure.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (1) Rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) Apply an amount of cleaning compound recommended by the cleaning compound manufacturer; (3) Rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds while: (a) Paying particular attention to removing soil from underneath the fingernails during the cleaning procedure, and (b) Creating friction on the surfaces of the hands and arms or surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms, finger tips, and areas between the fingers; (4) Thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Observed the kitchen hand washing sink was blocked with the soap dispenser and dishes when the inspector arrived. The items were removed from the sink during the inspection. Ensure that hand washing sinks are maintained accessible for employee use at all times.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed the sanitizer bucket and triple sink were testing at 0 ppm (Cl) during the inspection. After the PIC added bleach to both they were testing at 150 ppm (Cl). The PIC was reminded about the importance of testing saniztier concentrations on a regular basis and changing them frequently. Ensure that sanitizing solutions are always testing at the correct concentration.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

findings.title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
findings.comment: Observed various single-use articles (including, but not limited too, take out bags, to-go boxes, and containers) stored directly on the floor next to the cash register. The PIC was educated about storing single-use articles at least 6-inches above the ground to avoid contamination. Ensure that all single-use articles are stored correctly by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed there is bare wood screwed into the wall behind the front hand washing sink. The inspector educated that bare wood is not a smooth, durable, or easily cleanable surface. The bare wood must be sealed (ex. painted). Ensure that the bare wood is sealed to be durable, smooth, and easily cleanable by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
Observed the food handlers training of one of the employees is expired (the certificate expired in 2023). The only other employee at the facility is a CFPM. Ensure that all food handlers, other than those with CFPM certificates, obtain training in basic food handling principles. The employee must obtain their food handler certificate by the next routine inspection.  

410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.
